executiveSummary.text: Risk tone turned selective risk-off: S&P 500 7706.03 (-0.76%), Nasdaq 26936 (-0.69%), Dow 51511.6 (-1.03%), Russell 2000 2838.66 (-1.28%); VIX rose to 15.18 (+2.08%). The trigger was not earnings collapse but rates repricing: 10Y hit about 5.11%, its highest level since 2007 per CNN/Yahoo snippets.

Rates/USD are the regime control: 2Y 4.028 (+1.16%), 10Y 5.114 (+3.04%), 30Y 5.401 (+1.98%), DXY 101.115 (+0.68%). Base case 50% choppy/range-bound equities while yields stay near 5%; 30% further de-rating if yields/oil re-accelerate; 20% relief rally if Fed rhetoric softens. Confidence: medium.

AI/semis paused after a strong run: Brave/CNBC/TipRanks snippets show chip-stock rebound failed, with AMD/Broadcom/Intel slipping while ASML and KLAC were relative bright spots. This looks like discount-rate/positioning pressure more than evidence of broken AI capex demand.

Commodities were not a simple safe-haven trade: gold 4324.6 (-1.18%), silver 64.885 (-1.59%), WTI 92.16 (-2.57%), copper 6.785 (+0.38%), URNM 50.62 (-2.65%). Strong USD and higher real/nominal yields overwhelmed precious-metal momentum; oil fell even as Hormuz/China-Iran headlines stayed live.

Singapore was defensive but not immune: Business Times reported STI -0.2% as OCBC/Seatrium weighed; local banks were mixed and S-REITs remain tied to global yield direction. For KL, banks remain income ballast; REIT adds should wait for clearer 10Y/yield rollover.

Portfolio add-on: GOOG was the only large single-name breach at 334.98 (-3.58%); SLV 58.16 (-4.23%) and URNM 50.62 (-2.65%) breached ETF/commodity thresholds, while MLT 1.12 (+1.82%) moved positively. None appears to damage KL's long-term scarcity/AI-barbell thesis, but GOOG flags AI-capex/regulatory sensitivity.

usGlobal.what: US indices closed lower; small-caps and Dow lagged
usGlobal.why: Higher long yields and hawkish Fed/inflation concerns raised the equity discount rate; CNBC said the chip rebound failed and Yahoo/CNN noted 10Y yield pressure.
usGlobal.implication: Treat rallies as quality/selectivity rallies, not broad beta confirmation, unless 10Y stabilizes below ~5%.

ratesMacro.why: Markets repriced a higher-for-longer/hike-risk path after hot inflation and Fed-comment concerns in last-24h snippets.
ratesMacro.implication: Long-duration tech, REITs and precious metals face valuation headwinds; KL cash at ~4% retains option value.

asiaSingapore.what: Singapore stocks dipped modestly; Business Times reported STI -0.2% with OCBC and Seatrium weighing
asiaSingapore.why: Local tape is being pulled by global yields and stock-specific drags rather than domestic stress.
asiaSingapore.implication: Banks are still ballast; REITs need yield relief before aggressive adds.

commodities.what: Gold/silver corrected; oil fell; copper held firmer
commodities.why: Dollar and yields dominated precious metals; oil price action did not confirm worst-case Hormuz panic despite shipping/geopolitical headlines.
commodities.implication: Scarcity basket remains strategic, but add discipline matters when real yields/USD rise.

geopolitics.what: Iran/Hormuz/China oil channels remain the main geopolitical market transmission path
geopolitics.why: OilPrice/Schwab snippets cite Hormuz workarounds, elevated shipping costs and Chinese Iranian-oil leverage before Trump-Xi diplomacy.
geopolitics.implication: Market impact flows through oil inflation -> yields/Fed expectations -> equity multiples, not simply “geopolitics = gold up”.

moves.why: Yahoo/TradingKey snippets cite weaker sentiment ahead of Meta Connect, competitive AI pressure, elevated AI capex-return skepticism and ongoing antitrust/regulatory uncertainty.
moves.implication: Thesis not broken, but market is demanding proof that AI spend preserves search/cloud economics instead of just raising capex intensity. 2nd order: lower GOOG multiple can pressure mega-cap indices; 3rd order: if hyperscaler ROI doubt spreads, semicap orders could be questioned.
moves.action: HOLD; add only on evidence Cloud/search monetization is intact or on a deeper valuation reset; invalidator is sustained share loss in search/cloud plus rising capex with no margin path.

moves.what: SLV fell -4.23% and silver futures fell -1.59%
moves.why: Benzinga/FXEmpire snippets point to firm USD, elevated yields and hawkish Fed commentary; this is a real-rate/liquidity move, not a collapse in industrial scarcity.
moves.implication: Silver is higher beta than gold; 2nd order is margin/stop-loss selling after a crowded precious-metals run.
moves.action: WATCH/IGNORE day-to-day; ADD only if real yields peak or SLV retests support with USD rolling over; invalidator is sustained real-yield breakout and industrial demand deterioration.

moves.why: No fresh thesis-breaking uranium headline found in last-24h search; move likely risk-off/profit-taking in high-beta scarcity exposure. Benzinga separately highlighted uranium as an AI-energy trade.
moves.implication: Long-term nuclear/data-center power thesis intact, but uranium miners are equity beta plus commodity beta.
moves.action: HOLD; ADD only on panic/liquidity selloffs or confirmed utility contracting; invalidator is policy reversal or sustained uranium spot weakness.

moves.why: Positive move despite higher global yields; may reflect local REIT-specific positioning rather than sector-wide rate relief.
moves.implication: Do not extrapolate one REIT bounce into an all-clear while 10Y remains above 5%.
moves.action: HOLD/WATCH; add S-REIT basket only if US 10Y decisively rolls over and SGD funding conditions ease.

thesisImpact.why: The day hurt duration-sensitive AI/precious-metal assets but did not undermine semis, EDA, power, copper or uranium demand drivers.
thesisImpact.implication: Keep scarcity exposure, but demand margin-of-safety when rates spike.

thesisImpact.why: At ~4% cash yield, KL is paid to wait during rates-led de-ratings.
thesisImpact.implication: Dry powder can be deployed into forced selling rather than headline chasing.
thesisImpact.action: HOLD cash; deploy in tranches only on predefined triggers.

narratives.title: Rates are re-taking control from AI momentum
narratives.description: AI earnings/capex may be fine, but at ~5.1% 10Y the market lowers the acceptable multiple for long-duration cash flows. 2nd order: even winning AI firms can fall if discount rates rise faster than earnings estimates.
narratives.source: CNN/Yahoo/CNBC/Brave last-24h snippets plus Yahoo Finance prices
narratives.priceImpact: Negative for duration; neutral-to-positive for cash and banks.

narratives.title: AI infrastructure trade broadens into power, not just GPUs
narratives.description: Chip-stock volatility does not change the structural bottleneck: data-center power, grid equipment, uranium/nuclear and copper remain downstream beneficiaries if AI capex persists.
narratives.source: Benzinga uranium/AI-energy snippet; AI semiconductor searches

narratives.title: Geopolitics matters through inflation plumbing
narratives.description: Hormuz/shipping disruptions matter if they lift oil and LNG costs enough to re-anchor inflation expectations; today oil fell, so the immediate transmission into Fed pricing was less severe than headlines imply.
narratives.priceImpact: Conditional: oil spike would pressure equities; contained oil reduces macro shock.

secondOrderEffects.text: Higher 10Y -> higher equity discount rate -> mega-cap/REIT multiple compression; 3rd order: wealth-effect and funding-cost drag can slow discretionary AI-adjacent capex if persistent.
secondOrderEffects.implication: Do not buy every AI dip automatically; prioritize balance-sheet winners and capex toll roads.

secondOrderEffects.text: Stronger USD + higher yields -> precious-metal liquidation despite geopolitical risk; 2nd order: miners/ETFs can underperform spot due to equity beta and stop-loss flows.
secondOrderEffects.implication: For GLD/SLV, watch real yields and DXY before adding.

secondOrderEffects.text: Oil geopolitics -> inflation expectations -> Fed path -> yields -> broad risk multiples; because WTI fell today, the market is not pricing maximum supply panic yet.
secondOrderEffects.implication: Escalation matters only if barrels/LNG/shipping costs transmit to inflation.

investment.thesis: Keep the AI-scarcity barbell: semicap/EDA/foundry + grid/copper/uranium, funded patiently from cash rather than chasing green days.
investment.trigger: Add in 3-4 tranches if QQQ/semicap holdings sell off another 7-12% while earnings/order commentary stays intact, or if 10Y falls back below ~4.85%.
investment.whyNow: Rates-led selloffs create better entry points without invalidating structural bottlenecks.
investment.invalidator: Hyperscalers cut capex materially or semicap book-to-bill/order visibility rolls over.

investment.thesis: Singapore banks remain income ballast; S-REITs are optionality on yield relief, not a rates-proof income substitute.
investment.trigger: Prefer banks on weakness; add REITs only after US 10Y/SGD rates roll over or DPU growth is clearly organic.
investment.whyNow: Global yields are pressuring duration while Singapore fundamentals remain stable.
investment.invalidator: Credit losses rise materially or SGD funding stress appears.

trading.thesis: Fade broad beta until 10Y stabilizes; use QQQ/SPY rebounds as quality-selection windows rather than leverage signals.
trading.trigger: Tradeable relief if VIX fails to break 17 and 10Y retreats below 5.0%; otherwise stay defensive.
trading.whyNow: Market is reacting to rates, not just company news.
trading.invalidator: Breadth expands and yields fall simultaneously.

trading.thesis: Silver/SLV is a watch, not a knife-catch.
trading.trigger: Consider small add only if DXY reverses lower and silver stabilizes after the >4% SLV flush.
trading.whyNow: The move is macro-liquidity driven; catching it before yields stabilize is low edge.
trading.invalidator: Real yields and DXY continue rising.

watchlist.trigger: Watch Meta Connect/AI assistant news, Google Cloud growth, TAC/margins and antitrust remedies.
watchlist.invalidator: Search share and Cloud margins remain resilient.

watchlist.trigger: Risk-on improves below ~4.85%; risk-off accelerates above ~5.25% with VIX >18.
watchlist.whyNow: 10Y hit the highest level since 2007 per CNN snippet.
watchlist.invalidator: Earnings revisions rise fast enough to offset discount-rate pressure.

riskWatch.name: Rates shock / bond-market pressure
riskWatch.description: 10Y around 5.1% tightens financial conditions and de-rates duration assets.
riskWatch.mitigation: Keep cash ballast; add risk in tranches only after yield stabilization.

riskWatch.name: AI capex ROI skepticism
riskWatch.description: Alphabet move shows investors are questioning whether AI spend protects or dilutes returns.
riskWatch.mitigation: Favor toll roads with pricing power; monitor hyperscaler margins/capex guidance.

riskWatch.name: Oil/Hormuz/shipping inflation channel
riskWatch.description: Current oil price fell, but shipping and supply disruption headlines can reprice inflation quickly.
riskWatch.mitigation: Watch WTI/LNG/freight rates; avoid assuming gold automatically hedges if USD/real yields rise.

keyEvents.text: CNBC: S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed lower as chip-stock rebound failed; stocks slid on inflation/rate worries.
CNN/Yahoo: 10Y Treasury yield reached ~5.1%, described as the highest since 2007.
Business Times: Singapore stocks dipped 0.2%; OCBC and Seatrium weighed on STI.
OilPrice/Schwab: Hormuz workarounds, China-Iran oil flows and diplomacy remain live energy-risk channels.

bottomLine.whatMatters: The regime is being set by rates/USD, not by a collapse in AI fundamentals. A 5%+ 10Y raises the hurdle rate for every long-duration asset KL owns.
bottomLine.whatToDo: Hold core positions, keep cash ballast, use predefined tranche triggers; prioritize semicap/EDA/grid/uranium/copper quality when forced selling appears.
bottomLine.whatToIgnore: Do not overreact to one-day GOOG/SLV/URNM moves or generic geopolitical headlines unless they transmit through oil, inflation expectations, USD and real yields.
